topic: Can I ride a bicycle to the Sydney Opera House?
passage: Bicycles and other non-motorised vehicles. At the Sydney Opera House we welcome more than 10,000 visitors each day. Recently we’ve experienced increased pedestrian traffic on site and a rising popularity of bicycles, scooters and skateboards. As the safety of our patrons and visitors is our first priority all non-motorised vehicles including, but not limited to, bicycles (including commercial bicycle tours and hired bicycles), segways, skateboards and scooters must be dismounted at the Opera House site boundary, and safely walked, carried or parked while on site. Our staff will be asking riders to dismount while on the Opera House site and these requests will be made under section 4 of the Sydney Opera House Trust By-law 2021 and compliance is mandatory. Penalties for non-compliance may apply. If you have a disability or mobility needs as a rider, please contact Accessibility in advance for an escort to be arranged near the Macquarie Street Gatehouse. This change will not apply to prams, wheelchairs or other mobility aids. The Opera House continues to promote and support sustainable transport by providing facilities on site to safely park bikes while visitors and patrons enjoy their visit. Bicycle parking is located beneath the Monumental Steps.

topic: Is the Sydney Opera House Tour accessible for visitors with mobility requirements?
passage: Accessibility. On this 1-hour tour you will walk up to 2.5km and climb and descend around 300 stairs. There is no lift access and no opportunity to sit and rest during the tour. Please expect to be on your feet for the full hour. This tour is not suitable for wheelchairs and walkers. If you use a wheelchair or walker, we recommend our Mobility Access Tour that runs daily, which follows a step-free route and is designed for visitors with mobility needs. Other walking aids (such as a single stick or crutch) may be permitted at the discretion of our team, but please be aware that the tour moves at a steady pace and cannot be significantly slowed. For your safety and comfort, and to ensure a good experience for all guests, we may need to move your booking to our Mobility Access Tour instead. topic: What can I bring with me on the Sydney Opera House Tour?
passage: What can I bring with me on the tour?. Where possible, please do not bring bags to the Sydney Opera House. Bags larger than A4 size will need to be cloaked before you can go on the tour. However we can’t store suitcases or large bags as our cloaking facilities are extremely limited. Cameras are allowed on the tour and there are plenty of photo opportunities throughout the entire tour. Your tour guide will advise you whilst on tour if photographs are not to be taken inside any venues. Please note there is no video filming on the tour.
